description: Worked on AC/DC power and control systems.
Excellent troubleshooting skills in digital circuitry, test equipment operation, branch circuit wiring, and diagnostic testing.
Installation of avionics LRU's and Flight gauges on flight line.
Installation of Avionics equipment (AFCS, HSI, ADI, HUD, etc.).
Theory of operation of Avionics systems and Test sets.
Maintained CRJ-700,900 according to FAA standards and procedures.
Repaired and replaced Avionics equipment as required for proper functionality of aircraft.
Wire Stamping and Cannon plug Termination and routing.
Installation of wire bundles and termination of grounding blocks.
Interpretation of electrical and mechanical schematics, blueprints and diagrams.
Diagnosed equipment malfunctions and completed repairs to restore equipment and maintain uptime.

education.degree: Associate of Science : Avionics Maintenance technology

certifications.name: FAA Corrosion Control Academic Achievement Award

matchmaking_summary: The candidate has extensive experience as an Electronic Technician with a strong background in A/C and D/C theory and troubleshooting skills, particularly in the avionics field. With roles ranging from entry-level mechanic to shift supervisor, they have demonstrated expertise in both hands-on technical repair work and supervisory responsibilities. Their ability to troubleshoot complex electrical systems is complemented by their thorough understanding of aviation regulations and standards.
